text:
maria: Quick check — Spring Boot service using RestTemplate to call Redwood API; started getting 401s in prod after rotating secrets. I verified the secret in k8s and the value looks right. Anyone seen this?

chris: Did you base64 encode the header correctly? For Basic auth we do base64("<API_KEY>:") — note the trailing colon.

maria: Yep, I construct header like:

```
String auth = Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString((apiKey + ":").getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
headers.set("Authorization", "Basic " + auth);
```

But curl still gets 401. When I print the secret via kubectl I see an extra blank line at the end of the value.

samir: Extra newline would change the encoding for sure. Try `kubectl get secret my-secret -o jsonpath='{.data.api_key}' | base64 --decode | hexdump -C` to inspect trailing bytes. 

maria: Ran that: shows `0a` at end — newline. Oops secret was added from a file that had a final newline. Fixing now.

maria: Quick fix: `kubectl create secret generic my-secret --from-literal=api_key=$(printf "%s" "$KEY") -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -`

chris: Nice. Also FYI Java's `String.getBytes()` will include the newline if present, so the base64 differs. Use `printf "%s"` or `echo -n` when creating secrets. 

samir: If anyone hits this again, add a tiny unit test: decode secret, assert last byte != 0x0a. Saved me once. :facepalm:

deploy-bot: Deployment staging/svc-blue rolled because secret changed — 1 pod terminated, 1 pod started. :white_check_mark:

maria: Thanks all — fixed in 5m. Leaving this note in case someone else trips on it.
